outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current status records show both runs passed all 19 samples, so there is no discordant outcome. The concrete task-solving difference is procedural: the parallel run delegated behavior probing to a child and then the parent implemented and verified a flat module set, while the serial run handled all probing and implementation itself, patched two local mismatches, and delivered a nested module set. Both strategies satisfied the evaluator.
parallel_contributors: The parallel child supplied behavioral findings to the parent before implementation, and the parent retained file creation, integration, and verification ownership.
The parallel parent verified samples and multiple edge cases, although its final response disclosed a remaining uncaught-stderr formatting gap outside the official pass set.
serial_contributors: The serial agent completed the same work in one trajectory and patched an argparse wording issue plus ASCII ulabel behavior before final acceptance.
The serial run's broad local comparison harness ended with MISMATCHES 0 before final delivery.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a flat library layout while serial used nested idna and cli directories.
Parallel disclosed a non-strict traceback text gap; serial's final local harness excluded script-name-only differences and reported no semantic mismatches.
